verdicts.trueWording: A stalled military campaign stuck in the dead of winter is also evocative and harrowing.
verdicts.note: Live locusmag page fetched raw (HTTP 200, browser UA). Sentence appears word for word in the A Dance with Dragons entry; both limbs (evocative, harrowing) present.

verdicts.trueWording: Scenes from the point of view of a certain famous dwarf
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim on the raw page ('are perhaps the baggiest in the novel, straining at times for sardonic effect'), but the page never writes 'Tyrion' - it says 'a certain famous dwarf'. Identification is unambiguous in context yet is the claim's wording, not VanderMeer's, so graded substance rather than verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: a huge, dense novel that devotes several scenes to bizarre and beautifully imaginative set-pieces
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the raw locusmag page in the A Dance with Dragons entry.

verdicts.trueWording: The general prose style is reasonable, although prone to repetition.
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the raw Wertzone page (HTTP 200, browser UA), in the paragraph following 'The book's conceit'.

verdicts.trueWording: It is not uncommon to see a phrase used and then re-used just a few paragraphs later.
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the raw page, the sentence immediately after the prose-style sentence of claim 738.

verdicts.trueWording: the attempt to give the text an in-universe origin (a young maester writing a brief primer on the world for the notoriously impatient King Robert Baratheon) makes for a less dry reading experience than it might have been
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the raw page in the third paragraph; every limb (in-universe origin, young maester, brief primer, King Robert Baratheon, less dry) is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: Yandel likes to cover almost every claim in the book with lengthy caveats.
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the paragraph beginning 'The other problem'. Yandel's status as the book's in-world author/narrator is established earlier on the same page ('the young Maester Yandel ... has written the book').

verdicts.trueWording: by sometimes describing an event as mythological or untrue, but when combined with the reader's knowledge of the novels it becomes clearer what conclusions the reader is being directed to
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the raw page at the end of the 'The other problem' paragraph. Claim's 'makes clear' renders the page's 'becomes clearer'; no substantive divergence.

verdicts.trueWording: The North gets short shrift, which is quite surprising, whilst the longest region chapter is given to the ironborn.
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the raw page; the preceding sentence supplies the disparity-of-information limb ('There is also an issue with the disparity of information given on different regions').

verdicts.trueWording: excerpts from his work are rare ... he does give us some of the more evocative moments in the book
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the raw page. The rarity limb and Gyldayn's status as the second, more authoritative in-world source are both stated. Note the page spells him 'Master Gyldayn' (apparent typo for Maester) at first mention.

verdicts.trueWording: The book's conceit is that the young Maester Yandel ... has written the book a sort of Rough Guide to Westeros and Essos
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the raw page (the page's own sentence has a dropped 'as' before 'a sort of').

verdicts.trueWording: Going in, I was expecting something a little on the dry side-but I was pleasantly surprised by the ease of Martin, Garcia, and Antonsson's prose
verdicts.note: Live blogs.slj.com returned HTTP 500 (WordPress critical error); verdict formed on the raw Wayback capture https://web.archive.org/web/20150205084238id_/http://blogs.slj.com/adult4teen/2015/01/08/the-world-of-ice-and-fire/ - raw archived HTML, not a summarizer. Quote verbatim in the blog preface, as the claim's page hint says.

verdicts.trueWording: their facility in conjuring epic conflicts and romances in the few sentences allotted to them in various entries
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the preface of the raw Wayback capture. Claim's 'each entry' renders the page's 'various entries'; the praised parties are Martin, Garcia and Antonsson.

verdicts.trueWording: the bulk of the book's first half is taken up by a reign-by-reign account of the Targaryen dynasty
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the signed review body of the raw Wayback capture; page says 'the bulk of' the first half, which the claim compresses to 'the first half'.

verdicts.trueWording: The second half sketches each of the Seven Kingdoms, along with accounts of the ruling families. This half has less narrative drive
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the signed review body. The comparand is implicit: the page writes an unmarked 'less narrative drive' immediately after describing the first half's reign-by-reign Targaryen account, so 'than the dynastic half' is the only available reading, not an explicit statement.
